subject: Hospitality
title: Farm to Table Movement
description: A quick, practical guide to Farm to Table Movement.

hook.text: Farm-to-table promises food travels from local farms directly to your plate. But not all 'farm-to-table' claims are real.

buildup.text: The movement began as a reaction to industrial food systems—chefs like Alice Waters championed seasonal, local ingredients.

discovery.text: Waters' Chez Panisse in Berkeley, opened in 1971, built its menu around what local farmers had available that week.

twist.text: Investigations found restaurants claiming 'farm-to-table' while buying from the same industrial suppliers as everyone else.

climax.text: Genuine farm-to-table is expensive and logistically difficult. It requires relationships, flexibility, and higher food costs.

punchline.text: A beautiful idea, often faked. Real farm-to-table is hard and costly.

quiz.question: Who is a pioneer of the farm-to-table movement?
options: Alice Waters with Chez Panisse in Berkeley
